term: total cause of a thing's being (TotalCauseOfBeing c x)
definition: TotalCauseOfBeing c x: c causes the whole being of x, not only its coming to be in a presupposed subject, as a creator would and a generator does not. Example: (on the creation account) the first cause of a creature. Non-example: the parent, which causes the child's generation from presupposed matter, and the particular existential supporter of the CausalPerfectionTransfer roles. It is not universality (DEF-UNIVERSAL-ESSE-CAUSE-SCOPE), which STMT-UNIVERSAL-CAUSE-OF-BEING-IS-TOTAL relates to it as an open premise, and not mere enabling or counterfactual dependence.
note: Stipulative analyst notion, attribution deferred. ST I q.45 a.1 (creation as emanation of all being) is where a source might be found; no claim is made here.
